newsitem.title: UK: UK retail sales growth slowed in September - CBI.
newsitem.headline: UK retail sales growth slowed in September - CBI.

text.p: British retail sales volumes continued to grow in September but at a slower pace than in August, according to the latest distributive trades survey from the Confederation of British Industry.
The survey -- which subtracts the percentage of retailers reporting lower sales from those reporting a rise -- showed a positive balance of 46 percent saying sales rose in September.
And with a positive balance of 51 percent expecting sales to rise further in October, retailers saw business remaining above average for the fifth successive month.
"The rate of growth in retail trade eased in September, disappointing companies' expectations of a further pick-up," said Alastair Esperon, chairman of the CBI's distributive trades survey panel.
"However, the underlying growth in volumes -- as measured by the three monthly moving average -- continues to hold up, as consumers remain confident," he added.

The volume of stocks held by businesses in relation to expected sales dropped in September to the lowest level since the survey began in 1983, implying growing consumer demand is set to feed back through the supply chain, Esperon noted.
All the sectors surveyed, except for off-licences, reported a rise in sales compared with a year ago.
Chemists saw the strongest rise in sales since December 1993 following a sharp slowdown in August and sectors linked to the housing market such as furniture, carpets and DIY continued to flourish.
Clothing retailers reported a slowdown in September, according to the survey, following strong volume growth in the preceding three months.
Wholesalers' business was seen as above average in September, though less so than in July and August.
The survey covers 15,000 outlets of firms responsible for about 40 percent of employment in retailing, wholesale and the motor trades.
